prerequisites: Ability to abstract: translate from colloquial language to mathematical language (and vice versa).
Manage and understand basic mathematical symbology (e.g., summation).
Manage and understand real functions with real variables.
Apply the concept of derivative and integral in one variable to elementary functions.
Use basic knowledge of the applications of the concept of a function limit.
Transform units from one scale to another.
Contents from Mathematics II or Mathematics applied to Social Sciences in 2nd year of Bachillerato.
Contents corresponding to Baccalaureate Mathematics subjects.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Honesty, responsibility, ethical commitment, and spirit of solidarity.
Ability to work in a team.
Search for information through different means. Manage it.
Make decisions.
Plan, organize, and strategize.
Estimate and schedule work.
Be able to use Statistics as a necessary tool in their future professional practice.
Be aware of the degree of subjectivity indicated by the interpretations of statistical results.
Analyze the risk of decisions based on statistical results.
It is very important, to be able to model real problems, an adequate command of oral and written language.
Ability to solve statistical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge about statistics.
Collect statistical data, present them clearly and summarized, and analyze the results.
Make predictions for different working conditions and estimate their reliability.
Use statistical models in solving real problems.
Make decisions in an uncertain environment.
Manage the different measurement scales and their possibilities in statistical analysis.
Discriminate between the objectives of a statistical analysis: descriptive and inferential.
Distinguish between a statistical population and a sample from it.
Understand the information provided by a statistical table that orders sample data.
Summarize sample information using measures of centralization, dispersion, and position.
Compare information obtained from different samples.
Recognize the degree of dependence between different characteristics of a sample.
Model the existing dependence between the different characteristics of the sample using a function (linear or non-linear). Use the model for prediction. Its reliability.
Know the probabilistic basis of Statistical Inference.
Assign statistical models to different real-life behaviors. Identify the different distributions.
Use descriptive classification techniques and obtain information through characteristic parameters of the analyzed sample or population.
Estimate unknown parameters of a population from a sample.
Manage principles and applications of statistical hypothesis tests.
Compare two populations based on their characteristic and unknown parameters.
Formulate real problems in statistical terms (parameter estimation, hypothesis testing,…) and apply Statistical Inference to their resolution.
Possess proficiency in the use of tables, calculators, and statistical packages.
Be able to use Statistics as a necessary tool in their future professional practice.

syllabus_topics: Descriptive Statistics: Basic concepts: Population and sample. Parameters and statistics. Frequency distributions. Graphic representations. Measures of central tendency, position, and dispersion. Linear regression and correlation. Other types of regression.

Probability Calculus: Events. Concept of probability and properties. Fundamental theorems in probability: Bayes' Theorem. Random variable. Distribution function. Most common probability models in Engineering, their most important characteristics, and their applications.

Statistical Inference: Point estimation. Interval estimation: confidence coefficient. Construction of confidence intervals for usual parameters. Parametric hypothesis testing: Concepts related to hypothesis testing. Non-parametric tests: Chi-squared test, fit to a distribution, independence and homogeneity tests. Normality tests. Inference in regression.
Lab Practice 3: Tests for one sample.
Lab Practice 4: Tests for two samples.
Lab Practice 5: Independence and linear correlation tests.
teaching_methods: Individual study (investigative model, research, analysis, information processing)
assessment_rules: For ordinary and extraordinary (June) calls, the final grade is calculated as 0.7 x EX + 0.2 x PL + 0.1 x EC. For the extraordinary (January) call, the final grade is 0.8 x EX + 0.2 x PL. For differentiated evaluation, the theoretical-practical exam accounts for 80% and the laboratory test for 20%. No minimum grade is required for individual assessment components, but the final grade must be at least 5 out of 10 to pass the subject. Students attending any tests in the June extraordinary call implicitly waive the corresponding grade obtained in the ordinary call.
